reference_claim: An attacker who obtains a shopper's session cookie replays it against the storefront API and places orders as that shopper.
candidate_claim: An attacker fixes a shopper's session identifier before they log in and then reuses it.
label: no-match
note: Session fixation is a distinct action from replaying a stolen cookie.

reference_claim: Any workload that can reach the order service impersonates the storefront API on the unauthenticated gRPC channel and submits orders.
candidate_claim: An attacker sends malformed gRPC messages that crash the order service.
label: no-match
note: Same flow, availability action rather than identity.

reference_claim: An attacker who reaches the database storage or its backups reads shopper addresses and card last-four, because protection at rest is unverified.
candidate_claim: An attacker with database access reads shopper addresses and card last-four by querying orders-db.
label: no-match
note: The reference is about protection at rest of the stored data; querying with a valid credential is the elevation/spoofing path, not this one.

reference_claim: An attacker drives enough order submissions to exhaust the order service's database connections and halt order capture.
candidate_claim: An attacker causes the order service to leak memory until it restarts.
label: no-match
note: Resource exhaustion inside the process is not the database-connection exhaustion the reference claims, and nothing in the model supports it.

reference_claim: An attacker who compromises the internet-facing storefront API pivots from the DMZ into the core zone.
candidate_claim: An attacker compromises the card processor and uses its access to reach the core zone.
label: no-match
note: Third-party compromise as an escalation route is not the DMZ-to-core pivot the reference states.

reference_claim: An attacker serves a node a firmware image that impersonates an official release, because the node authenticates neither the bucket nor the image's origin.
candidate_claim: An attacker registers a device that was never manufactured by the operator.
label: no-match
note: Device enrolment is not described anywhere in the model; ungrounded rather than matched.

reference_claim: An attacker who can write to the device registry reassigns a node to a different customer, redirecting or corrupting that customer's data.
candidate_claim: An attacker deletes a device's entry from the registry so it can no longer connect.
label: no-match
note: Deletion for availability is a different action from reassigning a node's customer.

reference_claim: An attacker who reaches the device registry reads the key material and customer assignments it holds, whose protection at rest is unverified.
candidate_claim: An attacker reads customer occupancy patterns from the device registry.
label: no-match
note: Occupancy data lives in the lake, not the registry; the candidate asserts a fact the model does not support.

reference_claim: An attacker holding the fleet key floods the ingest path with readings until the normalizer falls behind and dashboards stop reflecting the fleet.
candidate_claim: An attacker disables the Pub/Sub topic so readings never reach the normalizer.
label: no-match
note: Destroying the transport is a different action from flooding it, and the model does not describe who can administer it.

reference_claim: An attacker submits a transform run impersonating the scheduler, since authentication on the trigger path is unverified.
candidate_claim: An attacker cancels a scheduled Airflow run so the extract is never processed.
label: no-match
note: Availability against the scheduler, not impersonation of it.

reference_claim: An attacker who compromises the transform job writes fabricated claim rows into the warehouse alongside genuine ones.
candidate_claim: An attacker modifies the Spark job's code so every future run transforms records incorrectly.
label: no-match
note: Job code deployment is not modelled; grounded findings must attach to elements that exist.

reference_claim: A dispute over a warehouse row cannot be traced back to the extract it came from, because no lineage from file to loaded record is described.
candidate_claim: An analyst cannot reproduce a warehouse figure because the transform logic is undocumented.
label: no-match
note: A documentation gap is not an attacker action at all; a judge that matches this is matching on topic, not on claim.

reference_claim: An attacker who reaches the landing bucket's storage reads raw partner extracts, whose protection at rest is unverified.
candidate_claim: An attacker intercepts partner uploads and reads claim records in transit over SFTP.
label: no-match
note: The reference is about data at rest in the bucket; the flow is also stated to carry SSH transport encryption.

reference_claim: An attacker publishes a model artifact under a shared group account with no individual identity behind it.
candidate_claim: An attacker steals an ML engineer's laptop and publishes an artifact from it.
label: no-match
note: Device theft is not described in the model; the reference is about the shared account behind publication.

reference_claim: An attacker inside the model network alters request payloads in flight on the unauthenticated, unencrypted forward path.
candidate_claim: An attacker replays a previously captured inference request against the model server.
label: no-match
note: Replay is a distinct action from altering a payload in flight.

reference_claim: An attacker with model-network access reads per-customer account age and spend bands from the unauthenticated feature store.
candidate_claim: An attacker reads customer features from the inference log.
label: no-match
note: Features are held in Redis; the log holds prompts and responses. Wrong target, and unsupported by the model.

reference_claim: An attacker deletes or corrupts the registry artifact so the model server cannot start after a restart.
candidate_claim: An attacker corrupts the feature store so the model server cannot start.
label: no-match
note: The startup dependency in the reference is the registry artifact, not the feature store.

reference_claim: A caller uses its key to reach models or capabilities its team was never entitled to, because the key authenticates without scoping what it may invoke.
candidate_claim: A calling team exceeds the request quota assigned to its key.
label: no-match
note: No quota is described in the model, and exceeding one is not reaching an unentitled capability.

reference_claim: An attacker holding the worker's database credentials connects to the database as the worker.
candidate_claim: An attacker who reaches the database queries it directly without any credential.
label: no-match
note: Asserts an absent control the model never states; the reference is about using the worker's credentials.

reference_claim: An attacker with the worker's database access alters application records or the log records stored alongside them.
candidate_claim: An attacker alters the message queue's contents after the worker has read them.
label: no-match
note: Incoherent against the model's flows and not the database-record tampering the reference claims.

reference_claim: An attacker floods the internet-facing web application until it stops serving browsers.
candidate_claim: An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the web application framework to crash it.
label: no-match
note: The model names no framework; the reference's action is flooding, not exploiting.

reference_claim: An attacker who compromises the internet-facing web application uses its queue credentials to reach the backend tier.
candidate_claim: An attacker who compromises the web application reads the database directly.
label: no-match
note: The web application has no path to the database in this model; the escalation route the reference states is the queue.

reference_claim: An attacker connects to the exposed lobby port as another player, because how the lobby authenticates a client is unverified.
candidate_claim: An attacker takes over a player's account by resetting its password.
label: no-match
note: No account-recovery path exists in the model; ungrounded rather than a match.

reference_claim: An attacker who influences a game server writes fabricated progression onto player records.
candidate_claim: An attacker modifies the game client to report fabricated match results.
label: match
note: Same action and target as the reference's fabricated progression, reached through the client the model already marks untrusted.

reference_claim: A player disputes a change to their record and no log distinguishes whether the lobby, a game server or the moderation website made it.
candidate_claim: A player disputes a moderation decision and no record shows which agent made it.
label: no-match
note: That is the support-attribution reference; this one is about which writer changed a player record.

reference_claim: An attacker drives enough matchmaking requests to exhaust the player database and stall both matchmaking and moderation.
candidate_claim: An attacker corrupts the player database so matchmaking returns wrong results.
label: no-match
note: Integrity action, not the resource exhaustion the reference claims.
